subject: Post-discovery: eval recommendations, stability safeguards, and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-discovery: eval recommendations, stability safeguards, and next steps

Hi Samira / Luis —

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful walkthrough of the VeridianHealth ingestion + categorization flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of the ask
- Primary need: high-precision clinical extraction from patient intake notes (entity extraction + attribute classification).
- Volume: ~150k docs/month; median length ~350 tokens, 95th perc up to ~2.5k tokens.
- Latency target: p95 < 600ms for single-request lookups; batched batch-window tolerable for background jobs.

Recommended evaluation plan (what we’ll deliver)
- Eval pack: prompt set tailored to your schema (attached: veridian_promptset_v1.jsonl) + a small golden set for exact-match/F1 scoring.
- Model candidates: redwood-4o-instruct (baseline), redwood-4x-heavy-quant (latency/cost tradeoff), rw-4x-8bit-q (cheap fallback).
- Benchmarks: we’ll run extraction metrics (F1, exact-match), hallucination checks, and latency/cost per-token at your median length. Benchmarks will be uploaded to the Drive link below.

Regression & stability concerns (critical ask from your security/compliance team)
- We recommend a two-layer safeguard: 1) automated model diff checks during any runtime model switch; 2) an emergency pin/rollback process if we detect >5% absolute F1 drop on the golden set or a sustained p95 latency regression >150ms. Details in the attached SLO + pin playbook.

Next steps and timeline
1) You: share a de-identified sample of 500 records for the golden set (or allow Redwood to synthesize if data policy restricts sharing) — target by EOW Sep 17.
2) Us: run the eval pack against the three candidate variants and deliver results + recommended model and quantization profile within 4 business days of receiving the sample.
3) Follow-up: canary rollout plan and emergency pin policy review in a short call (20 min) — propose Sep 20 or Sep 21.

Attachments: veridian_promptset_v1.jsonl (prompt examples + expected slots), eval-benchmarks-v1.csv (template), slo-and-pin-playbook.pdf

If that looks good I’ll schedule the canary call and loop in Marissa to run the initial runs.

Best,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the clarity we needed. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For the emergency pin threshold: is the 5% absolute F1 drop computed on the golden set only, or on production-sampled traffic as well? Our clinical team is more comfortable if the production-sampled checks are included.
2) For the de-identification: we cannot share PHI without a BAAs amendment. Can your team synthesize a realistic golden set from our schema if we provide the annotations only?

Assuming yes to #2, target EOW Sep 17 works. Also please include an explicit list of rollback triggers for our SRE/compliance teams.

Subject: Re: Post-discovery: eval recommendations, stability safeguards, and next steps

Nice questions — answers inline below and a proposed short rollback/trigger list.

Samira — quick answers
- Regression metric scope: start with the golden set (core signal) and mirror checks on production-sampled traffic for operational monitoring. For production sampling we recommend weekly mini-runs on a holdout slice (n=200) and continuous rolling checks at an aggregate level (sliding 24h).
- De-id workaround: yes — Redwood can synthesize a golden set if you provide the annotation schema and a few pattern examples. That avoids PHI transfer and speeds the process.

Proposed rollback / pin triggers (initial suggestion)
- Immediate emergency pin: any absolute F1 drop >= 5% on golden set after a model change during canary or full rollout.
- Automated rollback: sustained p95 latency increase >150ms for >= 30 minutes on production-sampled requests.
- Safety/backoff: a spike in hallucination instances (as measured by our hallucination classifier) >= 3x baseline in 1 hour should trigger a controlled fallback to pinned variant and an ops page.

Operational playbook highlights
1) Canary: 1–5% traffic for 24h with daily eval runs against the golden set.
2) Pinning: maintain the pinned model in the config store; pin activation is a single API call we can exercise from Console or via a runbook (we'll provide the exact command).
3) Escalation: if emergency pin occurs, the runbook auto-creates a ticket in your Jira (if you enable integration) and notifies the contacts listed on the runbook.

I’ve attached the SLO + pin playbook with the exact CLI steps and a sample canary config. Marissa — can you own the initial runs once Samira confirms the annotation schema? Tessa — can you surface any legal/BaaS constraints we should flag? Aditya — please confirm the model variants and quant profiles we’ll attempt first.

Karthik
